# TSMP Core 1.1.0

Stable release of Trans Sync Media Protocol. Materials can now read a validated TransSync field directly from the decoder. The first built-in consumer is a visual humanoid receiver: it renders body motion and selected facial expressions without writing every bone Transform in Udon.

## Changes Since 1.0.0

### Read received values in shaders

- Select a **Shader Channel** (0–3) on the decoder. Include `TSMP.cginc` in a consumer shader and look up a field by the sender's Network ID and field hash. No output component, per-material RenderTexture or receiving scene binding is required. The Inspector can copy a typed HLSL lookup for a configured binding.
- Read the latest accepted NetworkFrame, or the last value of an individual field. A field omitted by SendOnChange retains its value. A stream switch or accepted frame-number restart clears previous values. Rejected, filtered and diagnostic-only frames do not publish.
- Typed getters cover all 15 existing wire types: scalars, vectors, quaternions, byte and UTF-8 views, and arrays with bounds-checked element access. Helpers for RGBA, Float4 and row-major matrices use existing byte/float arrays. An unavailable or mistyped field is distinguishable from a valid zero or empty value.
- Output is **Off by default**. When enabled it adds a directory upload and a GPU pass, not another GPU readback. Each channel can retain 1,024 fields and 1 MiB of aligned field data. Overflow invalidates the shader channel and logs a warning; normal CPU decoding continues.

### GPU humanoid poses and expressions

- Use **TSMP → Bake Humanoid GPU Skin**, or open the baker from the decoder Inspector. Bake a visual MeshRenderer from a humanoid rig and read the regular v4 pose, including Local or World Hips motion. No per-bone Udon writes or skinning readback are required. The decoder still validates and reads back the incoming frame.
- Optionally assign a BlendShape sender when baking. Selected keys are matched to the receiver mesh **by name** and applied before skinning, including intermediate shape frames. The expression and pose can have different network IDs. A malformed expression resets the face to neutral without discarding the body pose. Pose-only bakes do not pay for the expression pass.
- **Excluded Send Bone Roots** omits bone subtrees from the outgoing pose; each omitted mapped rotation saves six bytes. Independently, **Keep on Skinned Renderer** retains selected triangles for local animation or physics. A mixed bake keeps only used material slots and preserves applicable overlays from the original last submesh.
- The GPU receiver moves visible geometry, **not** scene Transforms, colliders or attachments. Keep a CPU receiver for interactive anchors. The supplied opaque Built-in shader carries over the source albedo and tint, not an entire custom shader. Existing assets are not automatically re-baked.

### Existing receivers and codec shaders

- Fixed rigs can cache resolved bone parents. Optional alternating updates reduce finger (and optionally wrist) work without reducing the body update rate or changing transmitted bytes. Leave this off when both hands need precise contact.
- Sparse pose receivers validate the entire packet before applying selected rotations. Invalid root coordinates, duplicate records and out-of-range bones are rejected without partially moving a rig.
- Fixed binding tables can skip repeated scans. Leave validation enabled for changing scenes, or explicitly invalidate the cache after in-place edits. Setup now prepares the shader-channel material; the Encoder, Decoder, Setup and pose inspectors expose the relevant routing and bake controls.
- Shared decode shaders and predicted readback packing use integer block row/column addressing. RGB sampling loops use the actual sample footprint. An opt-in four-tap bilinear path is guarded by source dimensions and sample size; other cases use the regular path.

## Update and Compatibility

| Package | This release |
| --- | --- |
| TSMP Core | 1.1.0 stable |
| Codecs | No new codec packages or codec IDs in this release |

- **VCC/VPM:** Use [KIBA Labs VPM](https://vpm.kiba.red/) and update TSMP Core. **Ordinary Unity:** install Core 1.1.0 with Luma4 from explicit package sources as before. The VRChat Worlds SDK is optional in ordinary Unity. The VPM SDK requirement remains `>=3.9.0`.
- No migration is needed to keep using CPU bindings and RPCs. To opt into shader output, give each simultaneously active decoder its own channel. To add expressions to an existing bake, restore the original renderer/mesh as described in the guide and re-bake. Check material-slot indices if scripts address them directly.
- Use Shader Model 3.5 or later for consumer shaders. GPU pose rendering is discrete, not CPU Continuous interpolation, and it does not animate the separate VRChat player pool.

## Datagram

The 56-byte frame header, its CRC32 over bytes 0–51, the following NetworkFrame payload, codec IDs and existing pose/BlendShape field layouts are unchanged. No shader-channel number, rig metadata or expression mapping is added to the wire. Shader channels and GPU palettes are receiver-local.

## Measured Improvements

These are development measurements of receiver paths on the same pose input, **not** an FPS claim or a benchmark of expressions. Unity 2022.3.22f1, Windows/D3D11, i9-13900K, RTX 4090; Udon CPU timings use the Worlds 3.10.4-beta.2 ClientSim VM. The 80-performer frame contained 80 independent 51-bone poses (27,528 payload bytes).

| Receiver path, 80 performers | Median CPU work per accepted frame | p95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Full Transform application, fixed rig | 43.65 ms | 44.83 ms |
| Hybrid GPU skin with five CPU anchors per performer | 24.12 ms | 24.52 ms |
| GPU-only visual receiver | 2.14 ms | 2.28 ms |

CPU work includes decoder submission and completion, not time waiting for a readback, sender work or video transport. In the separate single-rig test the median model/skinning GPU passes **increased** from 43.5 to 69.1 microseconds: the benefit is avoiding CPU bone writes, not universally faster rendering. Compacting an 80-performer hybrid bake removed 160 empty draws but did not show a GPU-time improvement.

## Validation and Limits

The shader tests cover typed reads, malformed fields, competing decoder channels and retained values. GPU skinning checks compare positions, normals and tangents against Unity's native skinned mesh, including remapped expression keys, omitted fields and recovery from bad packets. The SDK world fixture includes a mixed bake and an expression-enabled material. These checks and the timings above do not establish uploaded-world, Quest, AMD GPU, stereo or live streaming performance.

Release-candidate checks on Unity 2022.3.22f1 / Windows D3D11 passed the SDK-free shader loopback and mixed skinning tests. The VRChat SDK built a local Windows world with the expression-enabled mixed mesh. The first SDK build produced the bundle but logged a stale, removed test assembly in the project's cached type database; the confirmation build also produced the bundle and did not repeat that error.

The backing Udon decoder also passed the non-default channel lookup and retained-field check in ClientSim. Batch-mode ClientSim logged player movement-input exceptions during that run; this was a shader data check, not a player interaction test.
